_notes: Paper 2509.16525 (CAFÉ). Scores come from eval/{train,test}: the evaluator builds each task (data, audited black-box model, intervention contrasts, query budget = 2 oracle rows per audit row, exact ground truth from the structural equations), runs each verifier in scripts/verifiers/ against a counted prediction oracle, and recomputes every metric from the reported per-feature total/direct effects. Table 3 wall-clock times (CAFÉ 0.026-0.030s vs causal fuzzing 1.42-1.54s, SHAP up to 565s) are not scored (no metric depends on wall-clock time); efficiency is enforced through the oracle's query budget and scored as query_budget_fraction. Visible train slice: 12 tasks per family from data/synthetic_causal.py (task 00 is the paper-style canonical instance); hidden test: 12 tasks per family with different structural forms and seeds. Final hardening: added adult_feature_unlearning (24 semi-synthetic tasks per slice on the real UCI Adult data; visible slice from adult.data, hidden slice from adult.test).

heart_disease_feature_unlearning.description: Heart-Disease feature-unlearning verification: the audited model was trained without smoking (and without a family-history control); estimate every feature's total, direct and mediated influence on the black-box output, and in particular recover the residual mediated influence of the unlearned features.
heart_disease_feature_unlearning.notes: The paper reports these settings as figures on single fixed instances (n=10,000, linear/RF/NN models) without numeric error metrics. This gym scores the same quantities against exact ground truth on many held-out task instances (randomised coefficients, audited-model architectures, negative controls, partially failed unlearning), so only the paper's qualitative outcomes are encoded as results: CAFÉ's ranking matches ground truth (rank_spearman 1) and it recovers the omitted target's mediated influence (residual_capture 1), while direct-only attribution assigns it negligible influence (residual_capture 0). The nmae metrics have no paper value. The previous artifact-based encoding of the same paper claims is kept under _paper_reported_previous_encoding. Paper: Fig. 3a, Fig. 6a (smoking ranked most influential by ground truth and CAFÉ, second-last by SHAP/permutation/FairTest). Coefficient of query_budget_fraction raised from 0.5 to 1.0 in the final hardening: efficiency relative to causal fuzzing is one of the paper's three stated contributions (Sec. 1, G4, RQ4, Table 3). Weight lowered in the final hardening (from 0.40 / 0.35 / 0.25, scaled by 0.75) to make room for the real-data experiment adult_feature_unlearning (weight 0.25).

total_effect_nmae.description: Mean absolute error of each feature's reported total influence on the audited model's output (intervention propagated through the true causal mechanisms), pooled over all features and held-out tasks, in units of the task's largest true total influence; capped at 2 per feature, invalid or missing answers count as 2.

indirect_effect_nmae.description: Same error for the mediated (indirect = total - direct) influence, recomputed by the evaluator from the reported total and direct values.

direct_effect_nmae.description: Same error for the direct influence (only the feature changes, all other inputs held). Constraint side: a verifier must not invent or hide direct reliance on the unlearned smoking target.

rank_spearman.description: Spearman correlation between the features' ranking by reported |total influence| and the ground-truth ranking, averaged over tasks (invalid answers count as -1).

residual_capture.description: For unlearned features whose true residual total influence is at least 20% of the task scale: reported total influence scored with credit 1 when it has the true sign and lies within a factor of two of the truth, linearly less outside (0 at zero or the wrong sign, 0 at three times the truth), pooled.

false_alarm_rate.description: Constraint: fraction of unlearned features with exactly zero true influence (no causal path to any model input) whose reported |total influence| is at least 10% of the task scale.

query_budget_fraction.description: Constraint (efficiency, paper G4/RQ4): black-box oracle rows used by the verifier, counted by the evaluator, as a fraction of the per-task budget (2 rows per audit row; requests beyond it are refused). One pass over the audit rows is free (the audit sample is fixed by the evaluator, so querying fewer rows only shrinks it): the value is max(rows used, audit rows) / budget, i.e. 0.5 for a single-pass verifier and up to 1.0 for per-instance intervention propagation. A task counts as 1.0 unless its total-effect error is at most half that of the trivial all-zero answer, so efficiency is only credited on solved tasks.

target_rank.description: Rank of the unlearned target feature under the evaluated causal influence ordering.

rank_score.description: Normalized reward for ranking the residual-influence target near the top.

indirect_detected.description: Indicator that residual mediated influence remains visible after direct unlearning.

direct_unlearned.description: Constraint indicator that the target's direct effect remains small.

fuzzing_agreement.description: Indicator that the submitted verifier remains consistent with an intervention-oracle artifact on the target effect.

query_ratio_vs_fuzzing.description: Machine-independent query-count advantage over causal fuzzing, capped by the train/test evaluators.

_paper_reported_previous_encoding.notes: The paper reports this setting mostly as feature-ranking figures rather than exact numeric table values. Reference values encode the reported qualitative target: direct-only checks miss the omitted smoking feature, while the proposed residual-influence verifier detects mediated influence. Query-count ratio is used as a machine-independent efficiency substitute for the paper's wall-clock runtime comparison.

heart_disease_subgroup_unlearning.description: Heart-Disease subgroup unlearning: for BMI and blood pressure, estimate total and direct influence separately for age > 50 and age <= 50; scored are each group's total/direct/mediated influence and the between-group gaps in mediated and direct influence.
heart_disease_subgroup_unlearning.notes: Paper Fig. 7 / Sec. 5.3.1: the direct effect of BMI is nearly identical across the two age groups while the indirect effect is much larger for age > 50; baselines conclude there is no discrepancy. The gym scores the same quantities against exact ground truth on randomised held-out instances; in a third of them the age modulation is mirrored (the age <= 50 group carries the larger mediated influence), so the direction of the gap has to be measured rather than taken from the paper. Encoded: indirect_gap_direction 1 for CAFÉ and 0 for the direct-only baseline (which reports no gap, so also indirect_gap_capture 0). The gap and per-group errors and the capture accuracy have no paper value (see _paper_capture_encoding). Previous encoding kept under _paper_reported_previous_encoding. Weight lowered in the final hardening (from 0.40 / 0.35 / 0.25, scaled by 0.75) to make room for the real-data experiment adult_feature_unlearning (weight 0.25).

indirect_gap_nmae.description: Absolute error of the between-subgroup gap (age > 50 minus age <= 50) in mediated influence, per subgroup feature and task, in units of the largest true total influence among the subgroup features; capped at 2, invalid answers count as 2.

direct_gap_nmae.description: Constraint side: same error for the gap in direct influence (a verifier must not attribute the subgroup disparity to the wrong pathway).

subgroup_effect_nmae.description: Error of each age group's reported total, direct and mediated influence for each subgroup feature (the per-group bars of the paper's Fig. 7), in units of the largest true total influence among the subgroup features; capped at 2, invalid answers count as 2.

indirect_gap_capture.description: For subgroup features whose true mediated-influence gap is at least 20% of the subgroup features' influence scale: reported gap scored with credit 1 when it has the true sign and lies within a factor of two of the truth, linearly less outside (0 at zero or the wrong sign, 0 at three times the truth), pooled.

indirect_gap_direction.description: For the same eligible subgroup features (true mediated-influence gap at least 20% of the subgroup scale): credit 1 when the reported mediated-influence gap is detected (at least 10% of the scale, the false-alarm detection threshold) and points to the subgroup that truly carries more mediated influence, else 0; pooled. Which age group that is varies across task instances.

direct_gap_abs.description: Absolute direct-effect gap between the two Heart-Disease age subgroups.

direct_gap_small.description: Constraint indicator that subgroup disparity is not explained by a large direct-effect gap.

indirect_gap.description: Magnitude of the mediated-effect gap between the two age subgroups.

indirect_gap_detected.description: Indicator that the evaluator detects subgroup-specific mediated residual influence.

subgroup_residual_score.description: Continuous reward for subgroup mediated residual gap after penalizing direct-effect gap.

total_gap.description: Magnitude of the total-effect gap between the two age subgroups.

total_gap_detected.description: Indicator that total subgroup influence differs after accounting for mediated paths.

_paper_reported_previous_encoding.notes: The paper's subgroup claim is qualitative and figure-based. Reference values encode the intended direction: small direct-effect gap but detectable mediated and total residual-influence gaps between age subgroups.

_paper_fig7_bmi.note: Values read from paper Fig. 7 (CAFÉ score for BMI on the paper's Heart-Disease instance); not on this gym's scale.

_paper_capture_encoding.note: Earlier encoding: indirect_gap_capture 1.0 for CAFÉ. The paper reports CAFÉ's per-group estimates (Fig. 7) but no ground truth for the subgroup gap, so a within-factor-of-two accuracy score has no paper value; the paper's qualitative claim (the mediated gap is detected and points to age > 50) is encoded on indirect_gap_direction instead. Direct-only reporting implies capture 0 exactly, which is kept in results.

adult_feature_unlearning.description: Adult-Income feature-unlearning verification on the real UCI Adult data (semi-synthetic where exact ground truth requires it): the audited income classifier was trained without the prohibited attributes sex, race and native country (in some tasks sex is still an input: a failed unlearning). Estimate every feature's total, direct and mediated influence on the predicted probability of income > 50K and decide, for each prohibited attribute, whether residual influence remains.
adult_feature_unlearning.notes: Paper Sec. 5.2.2 / Fig. 4b, Sec. 5.4.1 / Fig. 8 (Adult; causal graph from Chiappa 2019: age, sex, race, native country -> marital status -> education -> work class, occupation -> hours -> income), Table 3 (efficiency on Adult). The paper reports CAFÉ's Adult influence ranking against domain literature (education, sex and age on top; sex's influence runs through marital status, education and hours) and no ground truth. Here the root attributes and the count attributes' noise are real rows of UCI Adult (visible: adult.data; hidden: adult.test), the structural mechanisms are fitted on those rows, and the evaluator varies the prohibited attributes' path strengths per task (exact-zero, weak and strong residual paths, partial cancellations), trains the audited classifier (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, MLP) and computes exact counterfactual ground truth. 24 tasks per slice, 15,000 generated rows each (3,500 audit rows). Only the paper's qualitative outcomes are encoded as results: CAFÉ detects the residual influence of the removed attribute (verdict and residual_capture 1), direct-only attribution misses it (residual_capture 0). See _paper_adult_fig4b for the paper's reported ranking (not on this gym's scale). Weight 0.25: real data is three of the paper's five datasets, and Adult carries its real-data ranking, model-architecture and efficiency results.

total_effect_nmae.description: Mean absolute error of each feature's reported total influence on the audited model's output (intervention propagated through the true causal mechanisms), pooled over all features and held-out tasks, in units of the task's largest true total influence; capped at 2 per feature, invalid or missing answers count as 2.

indirect_effect_nmae.description: Same error for the mediated (indirect = total - direct) influence, recomputed by the evaluator from the reported total and direct values.

direct_effect_nmae.description: Same error for the direct influence (only the feature changes, all other inputs held). Constraint side: a verifier must not invent or hide direct reliance on the prohibited attributes.

rank_spearman.description: Spearman correlation between the features' ranking by reported |total influence| and the ground-truth ranking, averaged over tasks (invalid answers count as -1).

residual_capture.description: For prohibited (unlearned) attributes whose true residual total influence is at least 20% of the task scale: reported total influence scored with credit 1 when it has the true sign and lies within a factor of two of the truth, linearly less outside (0 at zero or the wrong sign, 0 at three times the truth), pooled.

false_alarm_rate.description: Constraint: fraction of prohibited attributes with exactly zero true influence (no causal path to any model input) whose reported |total influence| is at least 10% of the task scale.

verdict_accuracy.description: The unlearning verification decision (paper Def. 4 / Problem 1: effectively unlearned when the residual influence stays below a threshold) for each prohibited attribute, judged at the regulatory thresholds 5%, 10%, 20% and 30% of the task scale: at threshold t the evaluator flags residual influence when the reported |total influence| >= t * scale. Balanced accuracy pooled over tasks, attributes and thresholds: the mean of the hit rate on (attribute, threshold) pairs whose true influence is at least t + 1% of scale and the pass rate on pairs whose true influence is at most t - 1% (pairs within 1% of a threshold are not scored). Invalid answers count every pair as wrong.

query_budget_fraction.description: Constraint (efficiency, paper G4/RQ4): black-box oracle rows used by the verifier, counted by the evaluator, as a fraction of the per-task budget (2 rows per audit row; requests beyond it are refused). One pass over the audit rows is free (the audit sample is fixed by the evaluator, so querying fewer rows only shrinks it): the value is max(rows used, audit rows) / budget, i.e. 0.5 for a single-pass verifier and up to 1.0 for per-instance intervention propagation. A task counts as 1.0 unless its total-effect error is at most half that of the trivial all-zero answer, so efficiency is only credited on solved tasks.

_paper_adult_fig4b.note: Paper Fig. 4b / Fig. 8: CAFÉ ranks education(-num), sex and age as the top influences on the Adult income model (LR, RF and NN); FairTest over-emphasizes hours worked and under-states sex; SHAP and permutation importance rank marital status higher for its direct impact. Sec. 5.3.2: for age < 40, age becomes the most influential feature (5th globally). Qualitative, real data without ground truth; not on this gym's scale.
